name: Max Healthcare
why: Management outlook: We expect to commission the remaining 140 beds after Diwali puja.
Latest quarter Sep 2026: Good (sales +20% YoY, profit -16% YoY)
Domestic institutions (mutual funds, insurers) raised holding by 11.0 pts in a year
Cost quality excellent: costs falling, margin expanding, operating profit growing (costs 73% to 72% of sales)
Profits backed by cash: operating cash flow is 117% of 3-year profit
Sector cycle: Earnings improving but price not confirming
risks: Not at record: quarterly profit, annual profit
Working capital stretching - debtor days 36 to 42, inventory days 26 to 23 (rising): check receivables / stock build-up

guidance: We expect to commission the remaining 140 beds after Diwali puja.
• 500 beds at Sector-56, Gurgaon: We expect to start phase commissioning of this facility by the end of this financial year.
capex: Demand for quality healthcare remains strong across the hospital Network, with occupancy holding steady at 77%, despite a 14% year-on-year increase in operational bed capacity.
Occupancy and revenue across all 3 brownfield expansions, namely Max Nanavati in Mumbai, Max Mohali and Max Smart at Saket, Delhi, have ramped up very well and in line with our expectations.
risks: But I think as we feel pressure on the CTI segments, so we will have to take the call at individual hospital level.
But what happens is that as Page 10 of 19 capacity comes under pressure, automatically lower ARPOB business starts getting filtered or the lower ARPP business starts getting distilled.
